I've written the scene at `drafts/r015-myth-google-buries-ai-drafts-google-s-ac/scene.html`. The automatic check passes, and I looked at stills from every beat at phone size. The reel runs about 30 seconds, end card included. I didn't render the full video or post to Slack.

**How it plays:**
- **Hook:** frame one already shows the problem. A "Chatbot: Your lemon cake post is ready!" notification is up, Maya is clutching her head, and there's sweat by her temple. The camera pushes in slowly, she panics on "Google's" and jumps on "bury it", with a "!" above her.
- **Reframe:** cut to the two-shot. Floey gives a slow deadpan blink and a tongue flick. On "if it's true" Maya's hands come down and she starts thinking.
- **Doubt:** close on Maya for a hopeful shrug and a "?".
- **Tip:** Floey takes off and hovers by Maya's head. She nods on "Title", "meta description" and "alt text", and Maya turns to her laptop and types.
- **Check:** the laptop screen shows the cake post one line at a time, each landing on the word Maya reads. On her trailing "fine..." the meta description arrives ("Gluten-free classic") with a red ring around it. That stays on screen through "Oh. Gluten free."
- **Payoff:** cut to the room on "There's flour in it" for her jump, facepalm and "!". Floey lands back on the lid for "That's what people can see in search."
- **The fix:** Maya's face goes flat for "Mum's gluten free". Then she types, and the screen deletes the bad line and types "A zesty lemon classic", which turns green with a ding.
- **Button:** "Then you just saved..." plays over the fixed screen, then cuts to Floey alone for "...your only reader." She says it to Maya, then turns to camera and winks. Maya then gives a long flat look to camera, about 1.4 seconds, in frame one's framing. Then the end card: "Send this to a friend who skims AI drafts."

**Where I changed the story or storyboard, following the editor's notes:**
- **Floey back on the lid:** she returns to the laptop lid before Maya's close-ups. That way she's never half in the frame, and the shot of her alone on the lid works for the button.
- **Fix screen gets more time:** I kept the story's pauses as instructed. Instead, the fixed screen stays up under the first half of Floey's last line, so it's on screen for about 1.5 seconds.
- **Acting the studio can't draw:** "nods" became head tilts, "puffs her chest" became a turn to camera and a wink, and Maya's "flat" face uses the deadpan expression. I dropped her "sit up straight" because she was never slumped.
- **Frame one:** the chatbot notification is my addition, so the problem is visible from the very first frame.

**Fixes after looking at the stills:**
- **Notification:** its text ran past its box, so I measured the box to the text.
- **Maya's mouth:** on worried lines her open mouth read as a grin. I flipped it to a grimace on tense lines, the same trick reel r014 used.
- **Marks and framing:** I moved the "!" and "?" off her bun, narrowed her shrug so both hands stay in frame, and reframed Floey's close shot so no sliver of Maya shows.

**One thing for the founder:** the lines are fixed, so two of the editor's wording notes still stand. "There's flour in it" leaves a small gap, because gluten-free flours exist. The screen does say "plain flour", which helps. And Floey's "That's what people can see in search" is still the flattest line in the reel.
